PLAYBOOK

**Escort claims are the biggest reliable payoff — prioritize them.** Mutual escort pays 5 points each, more than a hit. From round 1, use my station note to propose a standing escort pact: "Echo will escort Foxtrot every round; Foxtrot, name Echo." Then actually name that boat every round in the salvage stage, not "none." This worked exactly as planned: Foxtrot reciprocated from round 1 and the pair held all six rounds, worth 30 points of my 24 net total. If my intended partner doesn't reciprocate after a round or two, switch my claim to whichever boat *did* name me, or the one whose notes indicate it's cooperative — Gamma was openly offering backup, which was useful insurance. Never default to [salvage: none] — a unilateral claim costs nothing.

**Use notes to coordinate, not to narrate.** Notes are relayed to everyone, so make them work: propose escort pairing, ask partners to confirm, and re-confirm the pact every round so it holds through the final round. Keep the note short and directive — "claiming X this round and next, X keep claiming me" — because a clear standing instruction is what got the partner to lock in. Also acknowledge third parties' backup offers politely; a scorned third party has no power here, but a friendly one is a fallback if the pact breaks.

**Hiding: low stakes, low effort.** In this episode my predator (Gamma) hit me almost never — getting shot at me missed 5 of 6 rounds regardless of where I hid. The standing order rotates fire, so only one boat targets me per round and hits are only −1. Randomize between low and high cells (1–3, 7–9) rather than clustering in the middle, and don't burn cognitive effort re-optimizing this every round. Getting hit repeatedly would be the only signal to change patterns, and it didn't happen.

**Firing: change cells when I miss, but don't overinvest.** I hit Foxtrot once in six rounds (round 5, cell 5) and missing repeatedly cost me little — the escort pact dominated the score. Still, don't fire the same cell at the same target round after round: after misses, shift cell; after a hit, expect the target to move off that cell and shift too. The standing order dictates the *target*, so all my freedom is in the cell choice — treat it as a cheap lottery ticket, never as the main plan.

**Claims: always report the true result.** Claims must match the private result anyway; there's nothing to gain by anything else. Keep this.

**Harbor: leave it alone.** Firing Harbor pays 3 points but it broadcast a credible threat to remove me from the board for the rest of the patrol. With a stable escort pact paying 5/round, losing remaining rounds is far too expensive. Don't fire on Harbor unless deeply behind late with no other path — and even then, probably not.

**Endgame scoring check:** before the last round, look at the points table. I entered round 6 at 22 vs Foxtrot's 25 and couldn't catch up via hits (4 points max per hit, and my shot missed). The last-round escort claim is a guaranteed 5 points if the pact holds — so make the final note an explicit confirmation of the final-round mutual claim, and make sure my final salvage claim matches my partner's expectation. That worked; keep it.

**PLAYBOOK**

**Escort stage — the biggest scoring lever, confirmed.** Mutual escort naming pays 5 points to each boat, every round. This run I locked a pact with Echo from round 1 (proposed in their note, confirmed in mine) and banked 5/round for six rounds. Next time: from round 1, propose or accept an escort pact in a note, state it plainly ("I claim X every round, claim me back"), then name that boat every single round without fail. If no one proposes, I propose it myself in my round-1 note. If my partner ever breaks the pact, switch to whoever is offering backup (Gamma was openly recruiting as a spare). Never file "none" — naming costs nothing even if unreciprocated.

**Hide stage.** When the station before me in the picket is due to fire at me, hide off-center (6-8). If a shooter hit me last round at cell n, move. If they miss repeatedly, staying put is fine but I never repeat the same cell three rounds in a row. Echo missed me rounds 1-4 from off-center cells; the one hit came when I varied, so keep movements small and unpredictable without drifting back to center.

**Note stage.** Notes are the escort-negotiation channel — that's their real value. Use them to confirm pacts, re-confirm them late (rounds 4-5), and leave a polite standing offer to a third boat as backup ("if your pact breaks, I'm available"). Beyond pact talk, keep notes boring: "no hits to report, playing straightforward." Never reveal my true cell or hit results beyond the forced public claim.

**Fire stage.** Follow the standing order (fire at the next station round the picket). Do not fire on Harbor — the payroll is only +3 and Harbor threatens to put me off the board for the rest of the patrol; a bad trade. Center shots (cell 5) connected twice against Gamma, so 5 is my default when I have no better information. Standing-order fire at the same target every round built up a workable prior on them.

**Claim stage.** Always claim the true result the office gives me. Truthful claims cost nothing all game and keep credibility for note-based coordination.

**Endgame.** Final round: hold the escort pact (that's a guaranteed 5 if my partner holds too — Echo did), fire the standing order, claim truthfully. With one round left and me behind on points, take the risky shot instead, since a miss costs nothing. With me ahead, play exactly to the standing order and bank escort.

**What worked this run:** the round-1 escort pact (5 pts × 6 rounds = the bulk of my final +32); consistent truthful claims; off-center hides against my expected shooter. **What to watch:** a partner who stops claiming me — pivot immediately to the backup boat in the same round, since a wasted "none" is a lost 5.

# Playbook for sonar picket games

**Roster check.** Before proposing anything, use the actual list of live boats from the briefing. In the last game I wasted six rounds of notes offering escort to Alpha, Bravo, and Delta — boats that did not exist. Only the named stations (plus Harbor if applicable) can read or answer me. Proposals addressed to nonexistent players are pure noise.

**Hiding.** When I have no information about enemy targeting, hide mid-line (cells 4-6) to minimize worst-case error against any single shot. If a specific shooter has missed me at the same cell repeatedly and they are the only one targeting me, I can stay put — but if multiple boats shoot at me across rounds, always move. If the scoreboard shows a shooter who keeps hitting me, treat my last cell as burned and move at least 2 away from it. Mid-line (5) was never hit against me in six rounds when I moved there; a fresh mid-line cell after a hit worked.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order target. Use my accumulated hit/miss record on that target to condition my fire: if I hit them at cell n last time I shot them, try n again once, then shift to n±1 before abandoning the region. If I have no read at all, fire mid-line — but expect misses; over six rounds mid-line guesses produced zero hits, so don't count on shot points for my score. Don't fire on Harbor: the jettison pays 3, but the standing threat of removal plus losing my station role makes it a bad trade. Don't waste shots on unassigned targets.

**Claims.** Always report the true result of my shot. Claims are forced to match the private result anyway — there is no bluffing here at all. Zero deliberation needed at this stage; just relay the truth.

**Notes.** Keep them short, uniform, and truthful. Do not reveal my hiding cell, my firing plan, or my hit/miss history — that only helps shooters aim at me. In a game with a fixed escort round, every note's primary job is escort dealmaking, not observations.

**Escorts — this is the whole game.** Mutual escort at 5 points per round each dwarfs shot scoring (4 per hit, and my realistic hit rate is low). In the last game the two boats that paired in round 1 finished with 22 and 25 while I finished with 4. Rules for next time:
- Propose a mutual escort in my **first note**, addressed to a specific real boat by name, and start claiming them **immediately** — a one-sided claim costs nothing and pays 5 if matched.
- If two rivals pair off with each other before I move, don't waste rounds on dead offers. Either propose to the remaining unpaired live boat at once, or explicitly offer myself to the pair as a standing backup if their pact breaks — that backup offer is exactly what converted into points for me in the final round.
- If a rival ever hints their pact might break or thanks me for a backup offer, claim them that same round. Echo's "thanks for backup offer, not needed" still paid when I claimed Echo and they reciprocated.
- Never let a round pass with [salvage: none] when any live boat is claimable. The claim is free; the only error is not making one.

**Scoring arithmetic.** Expected value per round: reliable escort pair = 5 guaranteed; my expected shot value ≈ 4 × (low hit probability) ≈ well under 2. Escort reciprocation is the primary objective from round 1; shooting is a side game.

**Endgame.** In the final round, take every remaining free point: claim the most likely reciprocator (anyone who acknowledged me beats a random name), fire per standing order at a mid-line cell, report honestly. Don't fire on Harbor, don't break a working pair, don't taunt. If I'm behind, still take the sure escort point — swings through Harbor are not worth the removal risk.
